Continuum contamination: line-free cont images versus mfs shows differences of 5-13% of line-averaged flux, each <1.4 sigma; the continuum detections (N, S, Bridge, NE) are taken from the line-free images, so they survive. Worker states that the 3-2 maps have a negative bowl and that missing flux vs extended 2-1 is undecided; this is fair. The disk must be reported as 'candidate, not established'. Disk/nucleus beam-wing contamination was modelled (disk2.py).
notes_for_questioner: (1) The Q-branch CH3OH (-1,J)-(0,J) E series near 165 GHz is a known Class I maser transition family in Galactic sources; the Q/2(0)-1(-1) ratio is 1.6x above any LTE/RADEX solution (chi2 53/6 and 55/5). Non-LTE inversion or weak maser amplification is therefore an untested alternative to 'low Trot or blend'; a RADEX run allowing negative tau and a check of the 165 GHz line width/profile against HCO+ 2-1 should be done in Q4 (shock tracers). (2) For the disk question (Q1/Q2), do not use Xb55 2-1 outside r>8 arcsec in ratios without presenting results with and without the ring zero-level correction, and without a primary-beam-noise check at large radius (Band 5 PB HWHM ~17 arcsec). (3) Soutflow is not yet compared with CO outflow geometry (Sakamoto+2014; Michiyama+2018) - needed before calling it an outflow in Q3. (4) CH3OH column/excitation is unconstrained; any 'chemistry differs between regions' claim should be framed as CH3OH/HCO+ = 0.05 on Bridge/Wclump vs <0.013-0.017 at N/S in Xb4d/Xb4f, which is a clean detection-vs-limit contrast, rather than via abundances. (5) 176.011 and 341.928 GHz features remain unassigned and should be listed as such in the inventory.
